description: Curated Pathways — progressive disclosure (Directive D). A 5-document journey per topic: plain-English context → replication angle → full raw source. [prescribed: Master Directive D — never open with 52,000 documents]

journeys.title: The Aether Story
journeys.tagline: Five documents that trace the most consequential wrong turn in physics — from the 'null' experiment to the living thread that survived.

steps.label: The Experiment Everyone Cites
steps.context: The Michelson-Morley experiment (1887) is taught as the 'null result' that killed the aether. But the story is more contested than the textbooks say — and the measurement itself is the hinge of the whole wrong turn.
steps.replication: Re-examine the original experimental logic. What exactly did the interferometer measure, and what assumption does the 'null' verdict rest on?

steps.label: The Man Who Found the Wind
steps.context: Dayton Miller, the most careful aether-drift experimenter, spent decades re-measuring and found a small but persistent drift the 'null' verdict didn't explain. His 1933 model is the suppressed counter-evidence.
steps.replication: Miller's raw data and apparatus are documented — a modern high-precision interferometer could revisit the question with instruments he never had.

steps.label: The Mystery Named
steps.context: 'Ethereal Ether and Michelson's Mystery' — a modern reconciliation attempt: what if the aether isn't 'nothing' but a medium with properties the 1887 experiment was never designed to detect?
steps.replication: The conceptual reframe is testable: distinguish 'no aether' from 'aether with specific properties'.

steps.label: The Living Thread — Etherodynamics
steps.context: Atsyukovsky's General Etherodynamics (chapter abstracts, English translation) — the most complete modern attempt to rebuild physics on an ether foundation. This is the thread that survived the wrong turn.
steps.replication: Read the translated abstracts first; the full work is the deep dive. This is where the aether line went from 'refuted' to 'rebuilt'.

steps.label: The Full History
steps.context: Whittaker's 'A History of the Theories of Aether and Electricity' — the authoritative survey. The raw source that connects every step above into one lineage.
steps.replication: The capstone: read the primary history to see how the aether was dismissed and what was lost in the dismissal.

journeys.title: The Wrong Turn: Cold Fusion
journeys.tagline: Born in 1989, dismissed, suppressed, and resurrected as cavitation LENR. Five documents walk the full lineage — and the death certificate ties it together.

steps.label: The Transmutation Claim
steps.context: Adept Alchemy's cold fusion transmutations — the claim that palladium-lattice electrolysis both produces excess heat and transmutes elements. The birth of the modern claim.
steps.replication: The palladium-lattice mechanism is the 'wrong mechanism' the death certificate flags. Understand it here, then watch it get replaced.

steps.label: The Commercial Claim
steps.context: Andrea Rossi's E-Cat — the most public cold fusion reactor claim. Whether or not it works, its history is central to how the field was perceived and suppressed.
steps.replication: This page carries the full Wrong-Turn Lineage section — the death certificate rendered in place.

steps.label: The Patent Landscape
steps.context: Cold fusion patents — the legal record of a field that kept filing even as mainstream physics dismissed it. Patents are claims, not proof; the archive preserves both.
steps.replication: Patents specify apparatus — a starting point for what a replication would need to build.

steps.label: The Survivor: Cavitation
steps.context: Mark LeClair's nanospire cavitation jet machining — the surviving thread. The death certificate's 'wrong mechanism' points here: not metal lattice, but cavitation in water.
steps.replication: The retry_now line in the certificate names the modern instruments (micro-PIV, nano-calorimetry) that could test this cleanly.

steps.label: The Superwave Variant
steps.context: Dardik's Superwave cold fusion — a third mechanism variant. Together with LeClair it shows the lineage didn't die; it branched and resurfaced.
steps.replication: Compare the three mechanisms (lattice, cavitation, superwave) — convergence analysis across the lineage.
